titleDv: ޤާނޫނު ނަންބަރު 24/2022 (ކުނި މެނޭޖުކުރުމުގެ ޤާނޫނު) އަށް 1 ވަނަ އިޞްލާޙު ގެނައުމުގެ ބިލު
summary: This amends the Waste Management Act. Resorts, farms, fisheries and industrial sites must write and follow their own waste management plans, and can be fined up to MVR 50,000 if they don't. Bringing any kind of waste into the Maldives becomes an offence, and so does selling, using or recycling hazardous waste without a permit. Businesses not registered for GST must also charge the plastic bag fee. The law gives two regulators new names and adds definitions for hazardous materials.
whyItMatters: Resorts and industrial islands become clearly responsible for their own waste, and importing waste is banned. Shoppers at small shops not registered for GST will also pay the plastic bag fee.
keyProvisions: Section 12: managing waste on islands or areas given out for economic or industrial work is the responsibility of the owner or operator.

Sections 24 and 24-1: places doing tourism, agriculture, fisheries or industrial work must prepare and carry out an operational waste management plan that fits the national waste master plan and island or regional plans. Failing to do so can bring a fine of up to MVR 50,000 (section 63).
Section 44: importing any type of waste into the Maldives by anyone is an offence.
Section 47: selling, using, distributing, recycling or processing hazardous waste without a permit from the Environmental Regulatory Authority is an offence.

Section 35-1: the ministry must make sure businesses not registered for GST with MIRA collect the plastic bag fee, and publish rules on how the fee is spent within 1 year. 'Plastic bag' is defined to include oxo-degradable and degradable plastic.

Fines paid by councils, or for offences outside council areas, go to the Maldives Green Fund. 'Agency' is renamed the Environmental Regulatory Authority and 'Authority' the Utility Regulatory Authority throughout the law.
whoIsAffected: Resorts, farms, fisheries, industrial operators, waste businesses, small shops not registered for GST, and island councils.
